case_title: Pargan Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307, s.397, each read with s.34
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-2 injured eyewitness, PW-3 complainant eyewitness); extra-judicial confession to PW-1; medical evidence of gunshot injuries
confession: Extra-judicial confession to PW-1 (a community head); relied on, but the Court stressed it is weak evidence needing corroboration, and found it corroborated by the two eyewitnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Assailants shot dead the victim and then fired at the injured eyewitness, causing a traumatic experience; the victim was robbed of a money bag
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302, 307 and 397 IPC read with s.34; life imprisonment with Rs.50,000 fine each for s.302; 10 years RI with Rs.25,000 fine for s.307; 10 years RI for s.397; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld (judgment dated 13.12.2012)
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.34); attempt to murder (IPC s.307 r/w s.34); IPC s.397 (as convicted by the trial court and upheld)
neutral_facts: On 25 March 1999, the victim and a companion withdrew about Rs. 4 lakh in cash from a bank and rode their two-wheelers back towards their office, the companion riding ahead with the money bag. Near a market, a black scooter carrying two people approached from behind. The pillion rider fired a pistol at the victim, who fell from the scooter. The pillion rider then snatched the money bag, which also contained a cheque book, and the scooter turned back. When the companion tried to stop them, one of the accused fired at him and he was struck. The accused fled on the scooter with the money bag. The complainant, the victim's colleague, arranged transport for the injured persons to a civil hospital. Police who reached the spot found the victim's body and the injured companion, and took blood-stained earth and the victim's scooter into police possession. The post-mortem recorded a gunshot wound to the upper back, with severe haemorrhage and shock as the cause of death. The injured companion had multiple gunshot wounds on the shoulder, neck, face and mouth, and lost consciousness, regaining it four days later. Police were unable to trace the assailants for several years. In July 2006 a special team was formed, and police received information that the accused were responsible; raids at their houses did not result in arrests. On 2 August 2006 a local community head told police that both accused had confessed to him that they had shot the victim and committed the robbery. On 7 August 2006 police set up a naka and arrested both accused as they rode a scooter. The accused declined a test identification parade. Both eyewitnesses identified the accused as the men who committed the shooting and robbery.
attempt_completion: Completed (murder), with an attempt on the injured eyewitness PW-2
physical_harm: Victim Varun Kumar died of a gunshot wound to the upper back with internal organ injury; PW-2 suffered multiple gunshot wounds (shoulder, neck, face, mouth) and lost consciousness
financial_property_loss: About Rs. 4 lakh in cash taken in a money bag, which also contained a cheque book
motive: alleged: robbery of the money bag containing Rs. 4 lakh
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-2 (injured) and PW-3 (complainant); PW-1's extra-judicial confession evidence (accepted, but not essential); medical evidence of gunshot injuries
witness_credibility: PW-2 and PW-3 found credible: consistent accounts; 90 seconds was sufficient to observe the assailants; an injured witness's testimony requires a higher degree of credibility, met here. PW-1 (Pradhan of the locality) found respectable with no axe to grind
post_offence_conduct: Assailants fled with the money bag after the shooting; after arrest in 2006 both accused declined a test identification parade
trial_duration: offence: 25.03.1999; trial judgment: 25.09.2008; High Court: 13.12.2012; Supreme Court: 05.09.2014
legal_representation: For accused: A. Tiwari, Eliza Bar, Shree Pal Singh, Shiv Kumar Suri, Shikhil Suri. For State: V. Madhukar, AAG, Anvita Cowshish, Kuldip Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; challan filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Judge, Kapurthala, 25.09.2008): convicted and sentenced. High Court (13.12.2012): appeals dismissed. Supreme Court (05.09.2014): appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: PW-1 and PW-2 are eyewitnesses and PW-2 is an injured eyewitness, so there is no reason to disbelieve them; 90 seconds was sufficient to observe and remember the assailants; PW-1 was an independent and reliable witness; the claim that faces were shown at the police station was never pleaded below
defence_argument: Prosecution story was suspect; PW-2 and PW-3 had not known the appellants before; the incident lasted about 90 seconds, so identification after 7 years was unreliable; PW-2 was shown the appellants' faces at the police station, which is why no test identification parade was held; the appellants were falsely implicated
legal_principle_applied: Eyewitness identification after a long gap depends on the circumstances of viewing (the horror of the event); an injured witness's testimony needs higher credibility; extra-judicial confession is weak and needs corroboration
precedent_relied_upon: Balwinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) Supp (4) SCC 259 (on caution needed with extra-judicial confessions)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Assailants shot dead the victim and fired at the injured eyewitness, a horror scene causing traumatic experience
